claim: For throughput throttling, PutRecord rounds each record up to the nearest kilobyte, while PutRecords rounds on the cumulative sum of the records in each call.

rounds on the cumulative sum of the records in each call

evidence.quote: Remember to round up to the nearest kilobyte for throughput throttling calculations when using the single-record operation [PutRecord](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kinesis/latest/APIReference/API_PutRecord.html), while the multi-record operation [PutRecords](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kinesis/latest/APIReference/API_PutRecords.html) rounds on the cumulative sum of the records in each call.

claim: A large producer that can micro-batch or buffer records should use the Kinesis Producer Library, the PutRecords operation, or aggregate records into a larger file before PutRecord. If it is unable to batch, it should use multiple threads.

values.display: use the Amazon Kinesis Producer Library
use multiple threads to write

evidence.quote: If the customer can micro-batch/buffer records, use the [Amazon Kinesis Producer Library](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kinesis/latest/dev/developing-producers-with-kpl.html) (which has advanced aggregation logic), the multi-record operation [PutRecords](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kinesis/latest/APIReference/API_PutRecords.html), or aggregate records into a larger file before using the single-record operation [PutRecord](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kinesis/latest/APIReference/API_PutRecord.html). If you are unable to batch/buffer, use multiple threads to write to the Kinesis Data Streams service at the same time.
